tasks.title: Open the watch table
tasks.body:
1. In TIA’s left Project tree, under this PLC, expand Watch and force tables. Double-click Add new watch table. It is alongside Program blocks, not inside OB1.
  2. In the new table, click the first blank Address cell. Enter these six addresses, one per row. Leave Modify value blank.
  3. Click the glasses button above this grid whose tooltip says Monitor all. Read Monitor value. Press Ctrl+S to save the table; this step needs no download.
AddressMeaning
DB98.DBX112.7Closing command
Q44.0Closing output
DB94.DBX29.4Robot permission
I505.7Robot input
DB200.DBX38.2Servo selection
DB200.DBX49.3EUROMAP selection

Read only. Do not force or change any of these machine bits.

tasks.title: Match the closing bit to the machine
tasks.body:
1. Have the operator identify the start of a production cycle over the phone.
  2. Watch DB98.DBX112.7 and Q44.0. Record when they turn TRUE and whether there is another pulse later in the same cycle.

tasks.title: Match the robot return to cycle end
tasks.body:
1. Watch DB94.DBX29.4 and I505.7. Record the low state and the return to TRUE.
  2. Have the operator confirm whether that return is when the robot is done and clear. Save your photos/times in the notes. Do not mark a robot sequence verified from manual closing alone.

tasks.title: Record the three reporting conditions
tasks.body: Record production-eligible, robot-data-valid and abort conditions. Use this machine’s confirmed event bits. Do not copy the MM6 block unchanged to a legacy WinLC target; its clock instruction support and interface must be checked separately.

tasks.title: Enter the 12 CSI_Report tags
tasks.body:
1. You already opened CSI_Report [DB56] in your screenshot. Use that new empty DB if it is still the one you are editing. Do not alter an already-downloaded 60-field DB in place.
  2. Click the triangle beside Static. Click <Add new> underneath it. Static is a heading, not tag 1. The far-left row number does not determine a byte address.
  3. Type PreviousCycleSeconds under Name, Real under Data type, and 0.0 under Start value. Enter the other rows below in this exact order. Do not create PLC tag-table entries.
  4. For this new DB: Properties → Attributes → Optimized block access OFF. Press Ctrl+S, then compile it. Check the generated Offset column; the first tag should be byte 0.
TagTypeStartByte
PreviousCycleSecondsReal0.00
BetweenCycleSecondsReal0.04
PreviousBetweenSecondsReal0.08
CyclesThisHourDInt012
CyclesPreviousHourDInt016
CyclesTodayDInt020
CyclesPreviousDayDInt024
DayShiftCurrentDInt028
DayShiftPreviousDInt032
NightShiftCurrentDInt036
NightShiftPreviousDInt040
TotalCompletedDInt044

This is a new 48-byte layout. The old 60-tag ladder and Kepware addresses do not match it. DayShiftCurrent replaces Shift1Current; NightShiftCurrent replaces Shift2Current. Use the corresponding Previous names too.
fields: Confirmed CSI_Report DB number for these 12 tags

tasks.title: Create CSI_Setup with three bits
tasks.body:
1. Under this PLC’s Program blocks → Add new block, choose Data block → Global DB. Name it CSI_Setup, using automatic numbering. Do not overwrite an occupied name.
  2. Expand Static and add the three rows below. Leave Enable and WiringReviewed FALSE. StartupPending starts TRUE.
  3. Save the new DB. Put it in your CSI or CSI_Adders group; either folder name is fine. These are new reporting controls, not machine controls.
SectionNameData typeStart/default
StaticEnableBoolFALSE
StaticWiringReviewedBoolFALSE
StaticStartupPendingBoolTRUE

tasks.title: Create one ladder FB: CSI_Reporting
tasks.body:
1. Program blocks → Add new block → Function block (FB). Name = CSI_Reporting, Language = LAD, Number = Automatic, Add new and open → OK. Leave this new FB optimized.
  2. In the upper grid, expand Input and enter the five BOOL rows below. Do not add them under Static.
  3. Start with the clock section next. Each numbered network tells you which extra local variables to add just before you use them. There is no 60-row declaration list and no helper FC to build.
  4. Do not reuse a partially built old CSI_Reporting with another interface. Keep that project as a backup, and use this compact route in the new working copy.
SectionNameData typeStart/default
InputCloseCommandBoolLeave default
InputRobotPermitBoolLeave default
InputProductionEligibleBoolLeave default
InputRobotDataValidBoolLeave default
InputAbortCycleBoolLeave default
How to place a ladder instruction
  1. In CSI_Reporting, the upper grid is for local variables; the networks below are for ladder. Start with Network 1 and add new networks below it.
  2. For contacts/coils, use the LAD toolbar. Click each tag field and enter its name. Use a normal coil unless the recipe specifically shows (S) or (R).
  3. For MOVE, ADD, SUB, DIV, CALCULATE, CONVERT, T_CONV, RD_LOC_T or TIME_TCK, use the right Instructions pane, find that exact instruction and drag it onto the rung. Select its stated type and fill its pins.
  4. Use comparator boxes for ==, !=, <, >, <= and >=. Use DInt for the integer operands, except the ClockStatus comparisons use Int. Do not type the displayed comparison as a contact name.
  5. Use Open branch / Close branch for parallel paths. The rung drawing is a wiring recipe, not text to paste. Keep the order shown; save/compile after entering a complete section.

tasks.title: Clock and schedule
tasks.body:
In the same CSI_Reporting FB, build networks 1–24 in order. These are not OB1 network numbers.

Day shift: Mon–Fri 06:30–17:00. Night shift: Mon–Thu 17:00–06:00 next day. Weekday values are 1 Sunday through 7 Saturday. Off-schedule cycles are excluded.

Network 01 · Read the PLC local clock

First add these local variables in CSI_Reporting’s upper grid. Expand the named section; do not add them to CSI_Report.

SectionNameData typeStart/default
TempLocalNowDTLLeave default
TempClockStatusIntLeave default
|--[ RD_LOC_T ]--|

No condition: start directly at the left rail.

InstructionType / destinationPins

No condition: start directly at the left rail.

InstructionType / destinationPins

Connect ENO to a normal coil #DateOK.

tasks.title: Cycle and between-cycle timing
tasks.body:
In the same CSI_Reporting FB, build networks 25–45 in order. These are not OB1 network numbers.

State 0 waits for a known robot return; 1 times the wait; 2 times a cycle. ADD accumulates elapsed milliseconds. MOVE holds the result. Another close pulse in state 2 does not start a new cycle.

Network 25 · One-scan closing edge

First add these local variables in CSI_Reporting’s upper grid. Expand the named section; do not add them to CSI_Report.

SectionNameData typeStart/default
StaticPrevCloseBoolFALSE
TempCloseRiseBoolLeave default
|--[ #CloseCommand ]--[/ #PrevClose ]--[/ #Fresh ]--( #CloseRise )--|

Place this contact/comparison path left to right. A slash means normally closed.

PathPlaceTag / operands
1Normally open#CloseCommand
1Normally closed#PrevClose
1Normally closed#Fresh
InstructionType / destinationPins

tasks.title: Add the FB call after OB1’s existing logic
tasks.body:
1. Compile CSI_Reporting. Open OB1, go to the end, and insert a new network after the existing processing. Keep the existing FC900 / RobotMain call; the analyzed project had it in network 48.
  2. In a LAD/FBD OB1, drag CSI_Reporting into the new network. In the call dialog choose Single instance, name the new instance CSI_Reporting_DB, and let TIA choose an unused DB number. TIA fills its variables from the FB; do not type those again.
  3. If OB1 is STL, keep its language. Create CSI_Reporting_DB with Add new block → Data block → Type = CSI_Reporting. Insert the FB CALL with that instance through the editor. Do not convert the existing OB1 or paste SCL.
  4. Connect CloseCommand = %DB98.DBX112.7 and RobotPermit = %DB94.DBX29.6. Fill the other three pins from verified existing conditions below. Keep this call unconditional and only once per scan.
InputMeaning
ProductionEligibleProduction cycles to count; exclude setup/jog.
RobotDataValidThe input data being observed are current and valid.
AbortCycleThe observed cycle has been canceled. Normal waiting is not an abort.

Those three mappings are still unverified. Leave reporting disabled until they are resolved. Offline compile-only placeholders: ProductionEligible FALSE; RobotDataValid FALSE; AbortCycle TRUE. Do not use the old CSI_Run or a second observer call.

tasks.title: Add the startup reset and review retention
tasks.body:
1. Open the existing standard Startup OB, normally OB100. Append a network without replacing its existing logic. Put an unconditional Set coil (S) on "CSI_Setup".StartupPending. In an existing STL network the equivalent is SET followed by S "CSI_Setup".StartupPending.
  2. If there is no startup OB, use Add new block → Organization block → Startup and choose an available standard startup OB for this CPU. Do not create or modify an F-block.
  3. For persistence, retain the new report counts/held values and the FB Static period keys HourSaved, DaySaved, DayShiftSaved, NightShiftSaved together. Keep the startup flag in place so an unfinished timer cannot span a restart.
  4. For the first RUN load, do not change existing retentivity or accept an unexpected STOP. Nonretentive commissioning is acceptable, but counts will not be promised to survive restart.

tasks.title: Compile and review the changes-only load
tasks.body:
1. Compile all the new blocks and intended OB edits. Double-click any error in the Compile pane and fix it. Press Ctrl+S.
  2. During the site-approved change window, choose Download to device → Software (only changes). Read Load preview. Check the target CPU and every affected block.
  3. Expect only the new reporting blocks and intended OB edits. Cancel unexpected STOP, hardware/F-program changes, deletion or initialization of an existing machine DB. Keep the new Enable and WiringReviewed FALSE until the final checks.

The ladder recipe has not been compiled in TIA or run on the PLC. It only reads existing machine bits, but compile/load/scan effects still require review.

tasks.title: Enable reporting and check a complete cycle
tasks.body:
1. In a new watch table add "CSI_Reporting_DB".State, the setup bits and the 12 report fields. Monitor the FB online to check ClockOK, Allowed and the five input pins.
  2. Confirm local time, live configuration and the three reviewed machine conditions. With site approval, modify only "CSI_Setup".WiringReviewed and "CSI_Setup".Enable to TRUE. Use normal modification, not Force; clear the Modify cells afterward.
  3. The first unknown cycle is skipped to synchronize. Observe at least five normal cycles. One completion should store approximately the observed cycle duration and add exactly one to TotalCompleted. Extra closing pulses must not count.
  4. Create a real wait and check BetweenCycleSeconds, then check PreviousBetweenSeconds at the next start. State 1 means a known live wait; zero on the live field alone does not prove the machine is running.
  5. Confirm the weekday holds and hour/day boundaries in an isolated test or at the real boundary. Do not change a running production PLC clock for testing. Archive the finished project.

This simpler DB has no quality/history fields. The first observed hour/day/shift may be partial. After an outage, PreviousHour/PreviousDay mean the last observed period, not guaranteed consecutive history. CPU STOP/power-off time is not timed. All counters stop at their DINT limit. Held durations remain unchanged on a skipped or aborted cycle.

tasks.title: Use this machine’s verified report DB
tasks.body: After its reporting code is installed and tested, record that machine’s report DB and offsets. Do not copy MM6’s DB number or V2 map into this device. Existing server notes and earlier checklist records are preserved under Completed.

tasks.body: After its reporting code is installed and tested, record that machine’s report DB and offsets. Do not copy MM6’s DB number or V2 map into this device. Existing server notes and earlier checklist records are preserved under Completed.

tasks.title: Select the existing MM6 device
tasks.body: Back up the Kepware project. Select the existing MM6 device under the approved Siemens TCP/IP Ethernet channel. Use the map here only with that driver; a symbolic/OPC UA connection uses its own addressing. Do not change PLC protection to make a connection work.

tasks.title: Create the 12 read-only tags
tasks.body:
1. Under MM6, create or select the Production tag group. Choose New Tag. Enter its name and address from the table below, Float for REAL seconds or Long for DINT counts, Client access Read Only, and an initial 1000-ms scan rate.
  2. Start with PreviousCycleSeconds. Require Good quality in OPC Quick Client and compare its value with TIA. Then add the remaining eleven rows.
  3. Do not use the old 60-tag address table. This layout starts PreviousCycleSeconds at byte 0 and ends TotalCompleted at byte 44. Confirm the actual DB number and offsets before using any address.

DayShiftCurrent / DayShiftPrevious are day shift. NightShiftCurrent / NightShiftPrevious are night shift. There is no SchemaVersion or Heartbeat field in this 12-tag DB.

tasks.title: Verify the displayed values and save
tasks.body: Compare the readings with TIA, including day/night Current and Previous fields. Use bad-quality/stale indications when the PLC is unavailable. Zero live waiting does not mean uptime; the compact map has no BetweenActive flag. Save the Kepware project. The CSV is an address reference, not a promised import format.

schema.name: PreviousCycleSeconds
schema.description: Last fully observed production cycle, seconds.

schema.name: BetweenCycleSeconds
schema.description: Live known wait; zero means no active known wait, not proof of uptime.

schema.name: CyclesThisHour
schema.description: Completions in the current local clock hour.

schema.name: CyclesToday
schema.description: Completions in the current local calendar day.

schema.name: DayShiftCurrent
schema.description: Mon–Fri 06:30–17:00; holds until the next scheduled day shift starts.

schema.name: DayShiftPrevious
schema.description: The preceding day shift, copied when its next scheduled shift starts.

schema.name: NightShiftCurrent
schema.description: Mon–Thu 17:00–06:00 next day; holds until the next scheduled night shift starts.

schema.name: NightShiftPrevious
schema.description: The preceding night shift, copied when its next scheduled shift starts.

schema.name: TotalCompleted
schema.description: Accepted complete production cycles since initialization.

instructions.title: Static is the heading; add tags underneath it
instructions.body:
In a global DB, expand Static and type each tag on its own <Add new> row. The heading occupying screen row 1 is normal. Your first actual tag goes at byte 0; screen row numbers and byte offsets are different.

In CSI_Reporting, local variables go in the section named by that network’s small table. Do not enter local # names in the global report DB.

instructions.title: Placing the ladder instructions
instructions.body:
1. In CSI_Reporting, the upper grid is for local variables; the networks below are for ladder. Start with Network 1 and add new networks below it.
  2. For contacts/coils, use the LAD toolbar. Click each tag field and enter its name. Use a normal coil unless the recipe specifically shows (S) or (R).
  3. For MOVE, ADD, SUB, DIV, CALCULATE, CONVERT, T_CONV, RD_LOC_T or TIME_TCK, use the right Instructions pane, find that exact instruction and drag it onto the rung. Select its stated type and fill its pins.
  4. Use comparator boxes for ==, !=, <, >, <= and >=. Use DInt for the integer operands, except the ClockStatus comparisons use Int. Do not type the displayed comparison as a contact name.
  5. Use Open branch / Close branch for parallel paths. The rung drawing is a wiring recipe, not text to paste. Keep the order shown; save/compile after entering a complete section.
